title: Week 1
post:
Weekly retrospective


What went well this sprint?

Something that went well this sprint was that I was able to brainstorm plenty of potential topics I was interested in for this summative and I narrowed it down to a couple of options. My goal this sprint was to have picked my topic and started brainstorming but unfortunately I was quite indecisive and I’m still tossing up between a couple of ideas. The ideas however are ones I’m feeling excited about which is why I’m so indecisive. I really want to choose the right one considering this is such a long project. Despite not having decided I feel like I’ve made some okay progress.


What didn't go well this sprint?

Something that didn’t go well was my indecisiveness and lazy approach to brainstorming. Since it was the first week back from the break I did still feel like I was in holiday mode. I had gotten used to sitting around and doing what I wanted all day so I struggled to get back into routine. I was also out of Auckland during this time so that definitely contributed to it. The reason I didn’t get very far this week was because I really couldn’t make my mind up. Even now I’m stuck between a few topics and I’m not sure which one I want to do. I also noticed that my brainstorming process was a little lazy. I didn’t log many hours this week and it was mostly just class time but I was constantly brainstorming in my head. It probably wasn’t the most effective as it’s not the most rapid option but I did manage to get some interesting ideas out of it.


What did you learn?

A lesson that I learnt was that I should just commit to an idea and stick with it. Anytime I almost locked in an idea I started swaying towards another topic and doubting my decision. At this stage I’m leaning towards one of my first ideas which is nutrition so I really just need to have the confidence to pick an idea. I also need to get back into routine. I learned that being lazy over the break threw my routine completely off and I kind of forgot how to do certain tasks since I was fairly out of practice.


What will you do next sprint, with this lesson in mind?

Next sprint I will have more confidence in my decisions and I want to spend less time feeling indecisive. To improve my process for the next sprint I want to get back into a solid routine and spend more time prioritising this summative. My first step will be to create a daily to-do list and try my best to stick to it. I hope this will give me a clearer direction so less time is spent contemplating and feeling stuck. Something else I want to do going forward is to fully focus on brainstorming rather than doing it while multitasking. Other than in class I didn’t really spend any fully focused time on it and it was something I just did in my head while spending my time doing something else.

title: Week 2
post:
Weekly retrospective


What went well this sprint?

This sprint I was able to gain a little more motivation and direction. Something that went well was that I was able to overcome my research slump. There was a point where I was extremely stuck and not making any progress. It took me days but I finally realised by just simplifying my tasks, I could make it feel a lot easier and I was able to make more progress from that point. I wasn’t able to complete my goals of this sprint. Even though I wrapped up my initial research, I wasn’t able to get anything else done. I intended to have some interviews done or even to put out a survey but due to that slump and my poor time management I wasn’t able to achieve that.


What didn't go well?

Something that didn’t go so well was the research process. I got super stuck on it and there were days when I barely made any progress. The sources I was looking at were also very repetitive so although it was good to compare the information I probably didn’t need to look at quite so many similar sources. Unfortunately, my poor time management had a big part to play too. Everyday I would say to myself I’ll get this done this afternoon, then this evening and then suddenly the day was over. I think the main reason for this was lack of motivation and also not feeling bothered. The task felt tiring so I kept avoiding it all week.


What did you learn?

The main lesson I learnt was to break up my research into some key questions / starting points. I got really stuck on the research phase as my searches were still very broad. This made the whole task seem super daunting and I procrastinated it a lot. When I tried to overcome this slump I realised my problem was that I made the task seem more difficult than it was. I broke up the task into smaller questions and subjects I could research and this instantly made the task so much easier. Something else I learnt is that I shouldn’t just assume and actually ask. When deciding my target audience between students and women with PCOS (or now PMOS) I just assumed I shouldn’t do PMOS due to it being a health condition as well as difficult to conduct primary research. During the WIP I was actually encouraged to look back into it for my target audience as it was quite niche and would be an interesting direction. If I had just asked prior I wouldn’t be stuck deciding whether to continue with students being my target audience or if I backtrack and focus on PMOS instead.

What will you do next sprint, with this lesson in mind?

For the next sprint I will break up the tasks into smaller tasks. As I mentioned the whole researching phase was quite daunting and the only way I was able to overcome this was by breaking it up into smaller tasks. Not only does this make it more achievable but I also got a small sense of accomplishment after completing each task. This keep my motivation level high and I was able to get more done than previously. Although it seems obvious I will make sure to remember this for any more research and for next term too. Something I would also do next time and continuing this assignment is to ask for help when I get stuck. I guess I was a little shy about it but I would have been much better off if I asked for advice or help going in the right direction. It would have saved me a lot of time and help me realise how simple the process actually is. Going forward I need to get over that and just ask

title: Week 3
post:
Weekly retrospective


What went well this sprint?

Something that went well was that I was able to come up with a solution idea I was excited about. Ideating off of my original idea about a single serve meal kit I was able to expand on that idea to make it more unique and engaging. I was also able to complete 4 interviews which I got some very good insights from, some of which I was surprised about. I was glad to complete the interviews as I was feeling a little stressed and guilty about leaving it so late. I knew many of my classmates had already completed their interviews so I was pretty stressed about being left further behind.


What didn't go well this sprint?

Although it feels like I achieved more for my project this week I was still constantly behind on everything. Honestly I’ve had some personal issues and low motivation over the last couple of days and I keep telling myself I would work on this later that day but I always run out of time. Despite those reasons, the main reason I always ran out of time was due to distractions. I got pretty addicted to replaying Skyrim and what I thought would be a hour long break turned into a 4 hour gaming session! I really wish I was able to complete more this week as it will only increase my workload in future weeks.


What did you learn?

From this sprint I learned that I should try to minimise distractions. Other than for some personal reasons, my biggest downfall were the constant distractions and temptations. I would try to use playing Skyrim as a motivator and for a fun little break but suddenly the entire evening would be gone. I’ve learned that I should either set a timer for breaks or confiscate Skyrim until I have achieved reasonable progress for the day. From my last reflection I mentioned that going forward I would split my tasks up to make them easier to achieve. This went alright at the start of the week and I broke up my daily tasks to be quick and simple but I found that I lost motivation as the week went on. I think that method will still work and I will try it again next week but with a different mindset.


What will you do next sprint, with this lesson in mind?

Next sprint I want to lock in and spend a lot more time on this summative. I plan to actually try and follow my weekly plan more closely and again I will break up the tasks to feel more simpler and achievable. Going forward I will use video games as a reward rather than for what’s supposed to be a quick break. By minimising distractions I think I will be able to get a lot more done next week. I will also try my best to stay consistent throughout the week especially with the proposal presentation coming up. During the WIP presentation I was up late the night before making the presentation from scratch because I had been lazy all week. Despite being proud of my effort I still wish I had started sooner so I could have been less stressed and tired by the end of the week.
